summary:
Project Title: SPACE ECHOES – The Machines That Stayed Behind in Space

Project Story:
Our project explores the stories of human-made machines left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions. We focus on the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages and NASA's Mars rovers, Spirit and Opportunity. We explain their missions, discoveries and the important role they played in space exploration.


Project Website:
We also created an interactive, futuristic space-themed website to introduce SPACE ECHOES. It showcases the three missions, explains their discoveries, shares interesting facts and includes an interactive quiz and information about our team.

Our Main Aim:
To remind people that even after their missions end, the machines we send into space leave behind valuable discoveries and a lasting legacy.
details:
Project Details – SPACE ECHOES

Project Title: SPACE ECHOES – The Machines That Stayed Behind in Space

Team Name: TWILIGHT
Team Members: Fouziya Beegam.N, Leena .S, Sona V. S
University: Lourdes Matha College of Science and Technology

1. What does your project do or how does it work?

SPACE ECHOES is an educational website that explores human-made machines left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions. It focuses on the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages and NASA's Mars rovers, Spirit and Opportunity.

The website presents information about their missions, journeys, discoveries and scientific contributions. Visitors can explore different mission sections, learn interesting facts, compare missions and test their knowledge through an interactive quiz.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand.
  • Introduces visitors to important NASA missions.
  • Explains the scientific importance of machines left behind in space.
  • Encourages interest in astronomy, engineering and space science.
  • Provides an engaging learning experience through interactive website features.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our aim is to create awareness about the lasting contributions of space exploration missions. We want visitors to understand that even after a mission ends, the machines left behind represent important achievements and scientific discoveries.

We also hope to inspire students to explore space science, technology and future space missions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

  • Google Antigravity: Used to develop the website.
  • HTML: For website structure, if generated in the project.
  • CSS: For website design and styling.
  • JavaScript: For interactive features, if used in the project.
  • NASA resources: For researching mission information and obtaining relevant images.
  • Computer/laptop: For website development and research.

5. How is your project creative?

SPACE ECHOES focuses on a fascinating but often overlooked part of space exploration: the machines that remain on other worlds after their missions end.

Rather than focusing only on astronauts and successful landings, our website highlights the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages and the Spirit and Opportunity rovers. We combine educational information, realistic space photographs, an attractive futuristic design and interactive features to make learning about these missions interesting.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific accuracy: Providing reliable information about NASA missions.
  • Educational value: Making complex space-related information easy to understand.
  • Visual design: Creating an attractive, futuristic space-themed website.
  • User experience: Making navigation simple and convenient.
  • Interactivity: Including quizzes and engaging features.
  • Accessibility: Making the website responsive across different devices.
  • Time and resources: Developing the project using available tools and resources.

Our central message

Even when machines stop exploring, their discoveries continue to tell the story of humanity's journey into space.
